question: Which tube links the middle ear to the back of the throat to balance pressure?
explanation: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx, helping to equalize pressure and drain fluids. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h1)

question: What main process fails first in many common ear, nose, and throat infections?

options.B: Hyperactivity of the primary gustatory nerves
options.D: Rapid regeneration of squamous epithelial cells

explanation: When the tiny hairs and mucus layer stop clearing properly, fluid builds up and lets germs grow easily. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h1)

question: What causes a stuffy nose during a common cold?

options.B: Rapid destruction of the acoustic nerve

explanation: Inflammation makes blood vessels leak and glands pump out extra fluid, which swells up the nasal passages. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why does a simple cold often turn into a bacterial sinus infection?

options.A: The immune system completely stops producing white blood cells
options.B: Cold air freezes the protective cilia inside the nasal passages
options.C: Viruses actively convert normal flora into pathogenic bacteria
options.D: Mucosal swelling blocks sinus drainage pathways and traps bacteria

explanation: Swelling closes off the tiny openings where sinuses drain, trapping fluid and bacteria inside. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h2)

question: What type of hearing loss does a buildup of earwax (cerumen) cause?
explanation: Earwax blocking the canal stops sound waves from traveling through to the eardrum, causing conductive hearing loss. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h3)

question: What happens inside the inner ear during Meniere's disease?

options.B: Severe atrophy of the external ear canal

explanation: Meniere's disease happens when fluid builds up in the inner ear chambers, increasing pressure. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which tiny loose particles in the inner ear cause positional vertigo (BPPV)?
explanation: Loose calcium crystals, or otoliths, float into the inner ear canals and send false balance signals to the brain. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why does turning over in bed sometimes trigger a sudden spinning sensation?

options.A: Inappropriate stimulation of hair cells by floating crystals
options.B: Complete destruction of the auditory cortex in the brain
options.C: Sudden bacterial infection of the external auditory meatus
options.D: Accumulation of thick wax pressing against the eardrum

explanation: Head movement shifts loose crystals across sensitive hair cells, making the brain feel like the room is spinning. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h4)

question: Besides dead white blood cells and debris, what else makes up the pus seen on infected tonsils?
explanation: White blood cells cluster together with bacteria and dead tissue to form the white patches seen during tonsillitis. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why can a sinus infection in the cheek make your upper teeth ache?

options.A: Inflammation of the throat closes the main Eustachian tube opening
options.B: The roots of the upper teeth lie very close to the floor of the maxillary sinus
options.C: Increased intracranial pressure forces fluid down into the dental pulp
options.D: Infection spreads directly down the facial nerve into the mandible

explanation: The roots of top teeth sit right below the maxillary sinus, so sinus pressure easily feels like a toothache. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h5)

question: What are the soft, non-cancerous growths that form in the nose from long-term allergies?
explanation: Ongoing irritation and swelling inside the nose can cause soft, teardrop-shaped growths called nasal polyps. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h6)

question: What causes the airway to close up during sleep in someone with obstructive sleep apnea?

options.A: Relaxation of upper airway dilator muscles
options.B: Excessive drying of the laryngeal mucosa
options.C: Sudden paralysis of the diaphragm muscle
options.D: Complete cessation of brainstem respiratory signals

explanation: When throat muscles relax deeply during sleep, the airway can easily collapse and block breathing. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the most common type of cancer found in the throat and voice box?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma starts in the flat, skin-like cells lining the inside of the throat and mouth. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why do cancers high up in the back of the nose often first show up as a lump in the neck?

options.A: The nasopharynx has a dense network of lymphatic vessels that drain to the neck
options.B: Viral infections cause generalized swelling of all regional sweat glands
options.C: The primary cancer site migrates downward into the thyroid gland
options.D: Tumors in this region rapidly invade the carotid artery and form cysts

explanation: The head and neck have many lymph channels, making it easy for cancer cells to travel to nearby lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h7)

question: Infection around the eye (orbital cellulitis) most commonly spreads from which nearby area?
explanation: Sinus infections can spread easily across the thin bone walls straight into the eye socket. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why can a severe sinus infection cause swelling around the eye and trouble moving it?

options.A: Complete obstruction of the Eustachian tube altering intraocular pressure
options.B: Systemic allergic reaction causing generalized fluid retention in the face
options.C: Metastatic spread of abnormal lymphoid cells to the lacrimal gland
options.D: Direct extension of infection through the thin lamina papyracea into the orbit

explanation: The bone separating the ethmoid sinus from the eye is very thin, allowing bacteria to cross over and cause swelling. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h8)
